question.value: Do gas structures on galaxy-cloud scales in NGC5236 and NGC4321 show hierarchical hub-filament structures, gas inflows and gravitational collapse like cloud-clump and clump-core scales?

evidence.quote: We investigated the kinematics and dynamics of gas structures on galaxy-cloud scales in two spiral galaxies NGC5236 (M83) and NGC4321 (M100) using CO (2$-$1) line.
using CO (2$-$1) line
We use the combined 12m+7m+TP PHANGS-ALMA CO (2$-$1) data cubes
which have a spectral resolution of 2.5 km s$^{-1}$ and angular resolutions $\sim$2.1 $''$ and $\sim$1.7 $''$
We select two face-on spiral galaxies NGC5236 (M83) and NGC4321 (M100) from the PHANGS-ALMA survey.

analysis_steps.goal: Remove galactic rotation and fit local velocity gradients

method.value: Linear baseline per filament segment, and alternatively KinMS dynamical model subtracted from Moment 1; gradients fitted around intensity peaks

evidence.quote: Here, we eliminated the large-scale velocity gradient by employing a simple linear function for modeling.

evidence.quote: Given that NGC4321 and NGC5236 are good face-on galaxies, here we ignored the projection effect in velocity gradient fitting.

findings_qualitative.value: sigma-N*R slopes are shallower than 0.5, indicating slower-than-free-fall collapse

evidence.quote: the slopes of the $\sigma-N*R$ relations are notably shallower than 0.5

claims.hypothesis: Hierarchical hub-filament structures and inflows extend to galaxy-cloud scales
claims.experiment: Velocity gradients along FILFINDER filaments fitted around intensity peaks
claims.result: Gradients increase from large to small scales; boundary ~500 pc; implied masses 10^5-10^7.5 Msun
claims.finding: Clouds/complexes act as hubs in spiral galaxies

evidence.quote: The variations in velocity gradients at both small and large scales (with a boundary around 500 pc) align with expectations from gravitational free-fall

claims.result: Slopes shallower than free-fall (R^-0.8 vs R^-1.5)

evidence.quote: However, in the observation, $\nabla v \propto R^{-0.8}$, also indicating the slowing down of a pure free-fall gravitational collapse.

why_this_data.value: Face-on galaxies with strong CO(2-1) emission and continuous spiral arms

evidence.quote: They have strong CO (2$-$1) emission, presenting large-scale continuous structures (strong spiral arms)

limitations_admitted.value: Only line-of-sight velocity and CO traced mass are measured, so acceleration and central mass are underestimated

evidence.quote: We only measured the projection of the realistic velocity vector and hence acceleration, thus tends to underestimate the observed acceleration.

referee_caveats_inferred: Gradients depend on filament identification and segmentation choices that are not specified
Resolution differs between galaxies (51 vs 123 pc), possibly biasing scale trends
Free-fall interpretation is degenerate with galactic rotation, shear and magnetic support
